newsitem.title: AFGHANISTAN: Firing briefly breaks out in Kabul.
newsitem.headline: Firing briefly breaks out in Kabul.

text.p: Firing erupted across the Afghan capital Kabul after nightfall on Monday but lasted only about an hour, witnesses said.

Tracer rounds could be seen across the sky and the sound of anti-aircraft guns, small arms and machine guns as well as occasional artillery could be heard for about an hour from about 6.00 p.m. (1330 GMT).
There was no immediate explanation but it was reminiscent of 1992 when mujahideen guerrillas captured Kabul, unleashing thousands of rounds into the air in a victory celebration.
There were no immediate reports of casualties and calm returned to the city after the firing died down.
The Taleban, who took over the capital on September 27, last week enforced a 9.00 p.m. to 5.00 a.m. curfew on the city. Under Taleban rule the streets have been usually deserted after nightfall.

The Islamic Taleban have suffered serious military reverses in the past few days, losing key towns to former government military chief Ahmad Shah Masood. Masood's forces were within an hour's drive of the capital on Monday.
